name: Post-receptoral color-opponent neural signal
summary: A neural processing stage in which cone-derived signals are compared in opponent channels. This stage contributes to color vision but is not a wavelength-to-color lookup or a physical oscillator at an optical carrier frequency.

axis.notes: Temporal spectrum of post-receptoral neural activity; no optical carrier identity is assumed.

constraints: opponent processing compares cone-derived signals rather than assigning one color to one wavelength
temporal spectrum depends on stimulus timing, adaptation, retinal circuitry, and downstream processing

relationships.description: Cone-derived signals feed post-receptoral neural processing in which opponent comparisons emerge; the relationship is not a one-wavelength-to-one-color mapping.

evidence.locator: Theories of Color Vision and Stage Theory

relationships.description: Opponent neural processing contributes to the visual processing underlying hue perception, without implying that one opponent-channel value uniquely determines a percept in every context.

evidence.locator: Opponent Color Theory and Stage Theory

evidence.derivation: Webvision describes post-receptoral opponent processing as a neural stage of color vision. Atlas therefore records the downstream temporal spectrum as unresolved rather than copying optical wavelength or frequency onto the neural signal.
